articles.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
articles.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
articles.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Senate Bill Asks Labor Department for a Plan on PERM Premium Processing
articles.excerpt: Appropriators want a report within 60 days of enactment on a fee-based fast track for green card labor certifications that now average about 300 days — but no premium option exists yet.
articles.nri_angle: PERM is the first green card stage for most H-1B professionals, a heavily Indian cohort; a paid fast track would cut a roughly 300-day wait at the Labor Department stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saudi Qualification Verification Disruptions Slow Work Visa Processing, Fragomen Warns
articles.excerpt: The pre-entry degree-verification step for Saudi work visas is taking longer than usual, with some applications returned for resubmission and no official timeline for a fix — a delay that lands heavily on Indian recruits.

sources.label: Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

articles.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian workforces in the Gulf; a stall at the verification stage delays joining dates and travel for Indian recruits across sectors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Proposes PERM Overhaul: 90-Day Job Ads and Layoff Bars for EB-2, EB-3 Sponsors
articles.excerpt: The Labor Department's first major PERM rewrite in two decades would lengthen recruitment, end the Schedule A bypass and bar sponsors with recent layoffs. It is a proposal only — comments close January 19, 2027, and current rules still apply.
articles.nri_angle: PERM is the gateway step for most employer-sponsored green cards; Indian H-1B professionals in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog are the group most exposed to longer recruitment and the layoff bar.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Proposed rule published in the Federal Register (docket ETA-2026-0133)
Public comment period closes; DOL then decides on a final rule

articles.title: H-1B Workers Are Giving Up on US Tech Jobs as Fees and Delays Pile Up
articles.excerpt: Bloomberg profiles a Google engineer leaving for the UK on a Global Talent visa, and reports employers from IBM to Flywire rethinking US sponsorship as new charges and PERM suspensions stack up.
articles.image_caption: Yash Sharma, a Google software engineer from India, photographed in San Francisco. Bloomberg profiled Sharma as he prepares to leave the United States for the United Kingdom after six years on an H-1B visa.
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders are the largest group exposed to the new fees and PERM suspensions; the open PERM comment window through January 19, 2027 is the one dated action in the story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Marriage to an Indian Citizen Gives No Right to Stay, Delhi High Court Rules
articles.excerpt: Dismissing a US citizen's plea to convert her tourist visa into an X-1 spouse visa, Justice Amit Mahajan held that a foreigner's entry and stay are matters of sovereign discretion — and that a marriage certificate does not stop authorities from examining the circumstances.
articles.image_caption: The emblem of the High Court of Delhi on the court gate in New Delhi, with media cameras gathered outside. The court held that marriage to an Indian citizen does not by itself confer a right to convert a visa into an Entry (X-1) visa or to stay in India.
articles.nri_angle: Many diaspora families include a foreign-citizen spouse; the ruling confirms that marriage to an Indian citizen is grounds to apply for an X-1 visa, not a right to one.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Sikh Grandmother's Deportation, Bill Would Let Old Removal Orders Expire
articles.excerpt: Four California Democrats introduced the Protect Our Neighbors Act on Thursday, citing Harjit Kaur, 73, who reported to ICE every six months for over 13 years before she was detained at a routine check-in and deported to India.
articles.nri_angle: The bill responds to the deportation of a Sikh grandmother from California and would directly affect long-term Indian immigrants living in the US under old removal orders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Texas Governor-Elect Hinojosa Says She Will Rescind Abbott's H-1B Hiring Freeze
articles.excerpt: The Democrat told The Texas Tribune the freeze on new H-1B petitions at state agencies and public universities "does not make sense" — but it stays in force until she takes office on January 19.
articles.image_caption: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa speaks on stage at an outdoor campaign event. Hinojosa told The Texas Tribune she will rescind the state H-1B hiring freeze when she takes office.
articles.nri_angle: Texas public universities, medical schools and agencies are major H-1B employers of Indian professionals; the freeze and its promised January reversal directly set their hiring rules.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Malaysia Ends Visa-Free Entry for Indians From January 1, 2027; Applications Open December 1
articles.excerpt: Malaysia's Immigration Department will discontinue the 30-day visa exemption for Indian citizens from January 1, 2027. Applications open December 1, 2026 on the MyVISA portal — and it is your arrival date, not your booking date, that decides whether you need one.
articles.image_caption: The Malaysian flag flies on a pole outdoors.

sources.label: Immigration Department of Malaysia — MyVISA portal

articles.nri_angle: Malaysia is a top short-haul destination for Indian travellers — 1.56 million arrivals in 2025 — and diaspora families visiting or transiting will need a visa in hand for any arrival from January 1, 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Now Counts Stipend-Paid Work for Professors Seeking Express Entry
articles.excerpt: A temporary public policy effective November 17 lets university professors and lecturers paid through stipends, grants, bursaries or scholarships count that Canadian work toward permanent residence — while teaching and research assistants lose category eligibility.
articles.image_caption: The flag of Canada. Canada now recognises stipend, grant, bursary and scholarship pay for university professors and lecturers under Express Entry.
articles.nri_angle: Indian academics and researchers working at Canadian universities on stipends or grants can now count that work toward permanent residence, and should update their Express Entry profiles.

articles.title: Jeffries Pledges Early Action on Bill Protecting Children of H-1B Workers
articles.excerpt: The American Dream and Promise Act, which covers documented Dreamers who age out at 21, is one signature short of a forced House vote — and its Democratic leader says it moves early next Congress if it stalls now.
articles.image_caption: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who has pledged early action on the Dream and Promise Act protecting children of H-1B workers.
articles.nri_angle: The bill expressly covers children of H-1B workers who age out of dependent status at 21 — a central anxiety for Indian families in the green card backlog.

articles.title: Former Boxing Champion Jorge Linares in ICE Custody, Facing Deportation From US
articles.excerpt: ICE says the Venezuelan three-weight world champion overstayed a temporary stay that began in October 2023; his lawyers say he is authorised to be in the United States.
articles.nri_angle: The case turns on a distinction every visa holder in the diaspora needs to know: ICE states plainly that a pending application or work authorisation does not confer legal status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FAIR Defends $100,000 H-1B Fee in Ninth Circuit as Appeals Multiply
articles.excerpt: The Federation for American Immigration Reform's amicus brief argues the President's fee is unreviewable under the APA — but the fee remains blocked by two federal court orders, and nothing changes for employers filing today.
articles.image_caption: Courtroom One in the James R. Browning U.S. Courthouse in San Francisco, seat of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, where FAIR filed its amicus brief defending the H-1B fee.
articles.nri_angle: The fee fight now spans three appeals courts; for Indian H-1B workers and their employers the practical position is unchanged — the $100,000 payment remains blocked.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada’s Immigration Backlog Falls to 1.51 Million as IRCC Finalizes 3 Million Files
articles.excerpt: IRCC cut its inventory by 35,180 applications in September, but family sponsorships grew, and 22% of economic files are waiting for levels-plan space rather than a decision.
articles.image_caption: The national flag of Canada. IRCC finalized 3,001,860 applications in the first nine months of 2026 while cutting the number awaiting a decision to 1,508,675.
articles.nri_angle: The split between files in processing and files waiting for levels-plan space tells applicants in Canada’s system what kind of wait they are actually in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tacoma Attorney Sues USCIS Over H-1B Delay Blocking Work for Detained Immigrants
articles.excerpt: An Olympia nonprofit paid $2,965 for premium processing of its new attorney's H-1B petition. The complaint says USCIS missed its 15-business-day deadline, took no required action for months, and kept the fee.

sources.label: USCIS — Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing Service

articles.nri_angle: The case shows H-1B employers and workers exactly how the premium-processing clock works — and the federal-court route when USCIS misses it.

articles.nri_angle: US green card holders flying India-US via a third-country hub face transit-visa checks at the gate; this ruling says an airline that cleared the documents at booking cannot stop the passenger at the last moment without consequence.

articles.nri_angle: NRI seafarers, who spend months at sea and often lack standard overseas address proof, can now open an NPS Tier I account using their employment contract or discharge certificate.

articles.title: Judge Vacates Four-Year Visa Cap, Restoring Duration of Status for Students
articles.excerpt: A Massachusetts federal judge set aside the DHS rule in full, holding it arbitrary and beyond the agency's authority — F-1, J-1 and I visa holders keep the status framework they have used for decades.

sources.label: Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration

articles.nri_angle: India is the largest source of international students in the US; the vacated four-year cap would have forced Indian doctoral and master's students on longer programmes to seek federal extensions mid-degree.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Proposes Tougher PERM Green Card Test: 90-Day Recruitment, Two-Year Layoff Bar
articles.excerpt: A Labor Department proposal would end the Schedule A shortcut, triple the minimum recruitment period, and bar employers from sponsoring green cards within two years of similar-role US layoffs. It is a proposal only — comments run 60 days from November 17.

sources.label: US Department of Labor — Federal Register NPRM (RIN 1205-AC29)

articles.nri_angle: Nearly 60% of PERM applications are filed for H-1B workers, a population in which Indian professionals are the largest group; the layoff bar and Schedule A changes directly affect their employer-sponsored green card path.

articles.title: Kunal Bahl's 2007 H-1B Rejection at Microsoft Led Him to Build Snapdeal
articles.excerpt: The Snapdeal and Titan Capital co-founder recounts how a rejected petition in 2007 ended his Microsoft plan and started his company, incorporated days before he landed in India.
articles.nri_angle: A founder's first-person account of an H-1B rejection speaks directly to diaspora workers weighing a US setback against building in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Comment Window Closes on Plan to End Deference for H-1B Extensions
articles.excerpt: DHS proposes deleting the one regulation that tells USCIS to respect a prior approval when an extension changes nothing. The rule is still in force, and a final decision comes next.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) adjudicates Form I-129 extension petitions; the DHS proposal would end deference to prior approvals on extensions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals received 77.6% of H-1B continuing-employment approvals in FY 2025, so a fresh-review rule for every extension would land hardest on them and their employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lalit Modi Becomes a British Citizen, Leaving Extradition as India's Only Route Back
articles.excerpt: The IPL founder announced the citizenship at the Oxford Union on November 14. Sources say it grants no immunity but closes the deportation route India tried in 2012.
articles.nri_angle: The citizenship closes one legal route for a high-profile Indian case in the UK, a country home to a large Indian diaspora, while leaving the 1992 extradition treaty as India's remaining path.

articles.title: Canada Holds New Student Arrivals at 150,000 a Year Through 2029
articles.excerpt: Ottawa's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan locks in the reduced student intake for three more years — up to 150,000 new arrivals a year inside a 370,000 temporary-resident ceiling, with no country quotas.
articles.image_caption: A view of Ottawa, Ontario. Canada's 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan holds new international student arrivals at 150,000 a year through 2029.
articles.nri_angle: Indian applicants face three more years of competing for a fixed global pool of 150,000 new student places a year in Canada, with no India-specific quota.
